clauses.issue: Other party queries the use of Bolt Operations OU as the signatory.
clauses.clauseExtract: Bolt requires that all third parties contract with Bolt Operations OÜ in respect of our standard NDA. Bolt Operations OÜ is the main operating entity of the Bolt group and we want to ensure that the main operating legal entity enters into NDAs. The definition of "Affiliates" (in Section 1) in the NDA includes all subsidiaries (such as those in the other international locations) as well as Estonian parent company Bolt Technology OÜ, making sure that (i) confidential information disclosed by us includes information relating to such other group companies and (ii) any information received by us can be shared with such other group companies. The definition of Affiliates is also mutual on the third party so will encompass their subsidiaries.
fallbackPositions: Preferably we maintain Bolt Operations. However, if this becomes a deal-breaker and you cannot negotiate otherwise, then at your commercial discretion you may use another Bolt group company. However, note that this then results in a more narrow scope of protection which may only adequately cover sharing from the local subsidiary and on a local level.

clauses.issue: The other party wants a purpose included in the NDA.
clauses.clauseExtract: Bolt considers that all information that it discloses will be Confidential Information and therefore it does not require the parties to specifically designate a purpose for the disclosure as long as the other party undertakes to maintain the confidentiality undertaking.
fallbackPositions: There may be unique circumstances where a “Purpose” may be required by the other party. In such a case, at the end of Section 1 the following amendment option is permissible and can be added to the agreement by counsel: “The Confidential Information disclosed for the purposes of this Agreement relates specifically to [INSERT SPECIFIC PROJECT PURPOSE].” Please make a service desk ticket to legal advising the need for this change and please fill in the above sentence with a clear purpose statement.

clauses.issue: The other party wishes to share the Confidential Information with other parties such as employees, agents, professional consultants, accountants and legal advisors or individuals “that need to know” and what to define this in the NDA.
clauses.clauseExtract: Bolt does not require the other party to list all of the associated parties that it wishes to disclose the Bolt Confidential Information to as our NDA wording is sufficiently broad to permit such discloses to a third party of the other party: “Confidential Information” means all non-public information relating to Bolt or disclosed by Bolt or its Affiliates to the above reference company, its Affiliates or any third party of the foregoing, that is designated as confidential or that, given the nature of the information of the circumstances surrounding its disclosure, reasonably should be considered confidential. However, please be reminded that you are obligated to maintain the confidentiality undertakings when disclosing to a third party.
fallbackPositions: None. Direct the other party to Section 4 (Company Personnel) and the last sentence which permits an extension to additional third parties who may be the other party of the Confidential Information.

clauses.issue: Other party wishes to limit one or both parties Affiliates.
clauses.clauseExtract: Bolt’s corporate structure is organized in a manner that is both flat and complex, consisting of many companies/entities which are fluid enough that Bolt needs entities to share information freely in order to conduct business.  If we are limited to a single entity in a particular NDA, we are forced to request permission to share the Confidential Information or explicitly include additional entities in the existing NDA if we want to enhance a service or expand the business to involve another entity, and there is an additional risk that information would be shared with an Affiliate by someone not familiar with the NDA restriction. Additionally, we would prefer to have a broad enough NDA in place that we can freely use it across different business teams – especially when we’ve devoted time to negotiating agreeable terms.
fallbackPositions: None

clauses.issue: Other party requests to identify either or both parties’ Affiliates.
clauses.clauseExtract: The “Affiliate” definition is standard and with hundreds of subsidiaries we can’t accept the administrative burden of listing all Affiliates.
fallbackPositions: None

clauses.issue: Other party requests to add threshold (50%) for Affiliates.
clauses.clauseExtract: Bolt’s definition of Affiliate is based on the industry standard for describing corporate affiliates.  We can’t know what a company’s corporate structure is, and therefore can’t know the risk we take on when the company tries to narrow the definition. There are also corporate structures where there is control, but no ownership. When we are disclosing Confidential Information, we need to know that our information is protected.
fallbackPositions: You may elect to amend the clause to state that: “The term “control” means the possession, direct or indirect, of the power to direct or cause the direction of the management and policies of an entity, whether through the ownership of voting securities or otherwise.” Please make a service desk ticket to legal advising the need for this change if you have commercial approval to make it.

clauses.issue: Other party is an entity that does not have authority to bind its Affiliates.
fallbackPositions: None (unless a governmental entity in which cases may be considered through legal SD).

clauses.issue: Other party wishes to change the definition of the business day.
fallbackPositions: This is a commercial decision which you are at discretion to make.

clauses.issue: Other party wishes to expand or contract the definition of Confidential Information.
fallbackPositions: Expansion or contraction of the definition should be analyzed on a case-by-case basis taking into account other Bolt Affiliates that may be affected by such modifications.  Generally, the general definition of Confidential Information should not be narrowed, but the exemplary list may be edited for clarity. Please make a ticket to legal if this is an issue.

clauses.issue: Other party wishes to impose a marking requirement for Confidential Information.
fallbackPositions: Limited amendments may be available subject to legal approval. Sometimes a party will require that Confidential Information be marked “Confidential” in order to qualify as Confidential Information. Generally, Bolt does not accept this request because of the administrative burden it puts on the business owner, particularly where we are disclosing Confidential Information. Our internal policies/guidelines have not established this practice for employees to follow consistently. If necessary (strong business need and ownership to comply), we can accept this request but we may want to suggest that we carve out a defined or limited purpose of the NDA before accepting a marking requirement (e.g. specific meeting, business proposal, etc. to limit the marking requirement).  If marking and notification is agreed to Section 8 must be left intact (return and destroy of Confidential Information).  If Bolt will not be disclosing information then this requirement is much less problematic, but the NDA will need to be limited in scope. If a deal-breaker, please suggest the following to the counterparty as an alternative: “Information disclosed orally or visually to the other party and identified at the time as proprietary or confidential shall be covered hereunder if it is reduced to writing, marked as confidential, and transmitted to the Receiving Party within thirty (30) days after disclosure.” If agreed, please make a service desk ticket to legal advising the need for this change if you have commercial approval to make it.

clauses.issue: Other party wishes to modify, add, or delete the exclusions section.
fallbackPositions: None. This section is not generally met with opposition and should not be removed.

clauses.issue: Other party wants “breach of separate agreement” in (iii).
clauses.clauseExtract: Breach of a separate agreement is covered by “wrongful”.
fallbackPositions: Propose and agree on the following with the other party: “(iii) is disclosed to the Receiving Party from a third party, except where the Receiving Party knows or reasonably should know, that (a) such disclosure constitutes a wrongful or tortious act or (b) such information was acquired or disclosed in breach of an obligation of confidentiality.” Please make a service desk ticket to legal advising the need for this change if you have commercial approval to make it.

clauses.issue: Other party wants to add a disclosure to governmental entities under the Exclusions.
fallbackPositions: None. Confidentiality obligations still remain even if disclosing Confidential Information under an order to a governmental entity. Depending on the circumstances, the government will have limited or no confidentiality obligations. The NDA protects trade secrets.  For information to be protected as a trade secret, it must be kept confidential.  If information falls into one of these excluded categories, it can’t be protected as a trade secret. NDA isn’t intended to cover information that can’t be protected as a trade secret.

sections.title: Use and Disclosure of Confidential Information

clauses.issue: Other party asks that the Confidential Information should be tied back to a “purpose” rather than an ongoing business relationship.
fallbackPositions: See fallback points for the purpose above.

clauses.issue: Other party wishes to add export regulation terms.
fallbackPositions: Propose and agree on the following with the other party: “The Receiving Party will not export any Confidential Information in any manner contrary to the export regulations of the United States or the applicable jurisdiction of the relevant Receiving Party.” Please make a service desk ticket to legal advising the need for this change if you have commercial approval to make it.

clauses.issue: Other party wishes to add further protection language.
fallbackPositions: None. Bolt goes to great lengths to protect its Confidential Information and takes steps beyond those taken by many other companies. In situations where we are more likely to be receiving Confidential Information, the obligation to protect a third party’s Confidential Information to the same extent as we protect our own Confidential Information is a high threshold.

clauses.issue: Other party wants all Personnel to execute written nondisclosure agreements.
clauses.clauseExtract: Bolt employees and contractors sign nondisclosure agreements, so we can accept this position as to such Personnel, but not more broadly. The parties to the NDA are accepting responsibility for the treatment of the Confidential Information disclosed to their Personnel whether or not an NDA has been signed by their Personnel.
fallbackPositions: Propose the addition of: “and (iv) in the case of a Receiving Party’s employees and contractors, who have executed written nondisclosure agreements obligating them to protect the Confidential Information.” Please make a service desk ticket to legal advising the need for this change if you have commercial approval to make it.

clauses.issue: Other party wants to narrow the definition of Personnel to exclude some or all of directors, officers, agents, legal and financial advisers, or investment banks.
fallbackPositions: None. We should push back hard against such exclusion since in most cases when we are receiving Confidential Information we will want to share more broadly than just employees and contractors – particularly if the relationship or transaction expands beyond an initial narrow scope.

clauses.issue: Other party wants to replace “entities controlled by the Receiving Party” with “Affiliates”.
fallbackPositions: Bolt will accept this revision. Please make a service desk ticket to legal advising the need for this change if you have commercial approval to make it.

clauses.issue: Other party requests an unfettered right to make disclosures to certain governmental bodies or any taxation authority of competent jurisdiction if it is lawful.
clauses.clauseExtract: The government agency or authority may have disclosure as long as correct process has been exercised such as Bolt receiving a valid court order or official notice from the government agency or authority in general we would not seek to fetter any valid request for disclosure from a Governmental Entity. However, Bolt should be kept informed as far as reasonably practicable:
fallbackPositions: The Bolt standard language is broad to permit the other party to disclose the Confidential Information in respect of “orders of governmental entities” with jurisdiction over it. However, the Bolt standard is for the other party to notify Bolt prior to such disclosure which may cause friction particularly if the other party is under a legal duty to disclose which puts them in direct breach of the NDA if no notice to Bolt is permitted. Agree to insert the following at end of the Section: “If Company is unable to inform Bolt before Confidential Information is disclosed pursuant to this clause 5 it shall, to the extent permitted by law, inform Bolt of the full circumstances of the disclosure and the information that has been disclosed as soon as reasonably practicable after such disclosure has been made.” Please make a service desk ticket to legal advising the need for this change if you have commercial approval to make it.

clauses.issue: Other party wishes to use Bolt’s trade name, trademark logo or any other proprietary rights if the subject of discussion results in a commercial arrangement, partnership, project or user offering.
clauses.clauseExtract: Any request for use of Bolt’s trade name, trademark logo or any other proprietary rights following signature of the NDA will be permitted subject to the parties entering into a formal contract of which provisions will need to expressly supersede this section of the standard NDA.
fallbackPositions: None. This is not the purpose of NDA and an agreement independent of this will need to be reached specific to the IP.

clauses.issue: Request to add “known” in front of first “unauthorized” reference.
fallbackPositions: Can be agreed. Please make a service desk ticket to legal advising the need for this change if you have commercial approval to make it.

clauses.issue: Request to use “use commercially reasonable efforts to” in front of “cooperate”.
fallbackPositions: Can be agreed. Please make a service desk ticket to legal advising the need for this change if you have commercial approval to make it.

clauses.issue: Other party states that they may be under a professional or regulatory obligation to retain the Confidential Information.
clauses.clauseExtract: Bolt will accept the non-return of Confidential Information if you have a regulatory obligation to maintain our Confidential Information. However, the confidentiality undertaking shall continue to survive.
fallbackPositions: Other party may suggest they have a “professional obligation” as an alternative to the regulatory circumstance but we should test if there is no evidence to suggest this is the case. The other party will need to clearly explain the use case and the Bolt legal team member should verify that the other party use case is valid in respect of the applicable regulation. If it can be confirmed then the following can be added to the end of the section: “…unless otherwise agreed by Bolt, Company may (i) retain the Confidential Information as required by law or a regulatory obligation [including for audits] and (ii) copies of the Confidential Information held on IT back-up systems of the Receiving Party. ” In Section 11 include Section “8” as part of the Agreement that shall survive following termination: “…with respect to Confidential Information will survive for 3 years following termination of this Agreement, and Sections 6, 8, 9, 10, 11, and 12 will survive indefinitely and the confidentiality obligations of this Agreement…” Please make a service desk ticket to legal advising the need for this change if you have commercial approval to make it.

clauses.issue: Other party seeks to retain Confidential Information.
fallbackPositions: In general, Bolt maintains an extremely strong position against another party retaining a copy of any of our Confidential Information after the business purpose is completed or terminated.  We should ask what the purpose would be for them to keep our Confidential Information. Our concern is that if a party keeps a copy of our Confidential Information, in any form, and our relationship ends, the copy of the information they’ve kept may be subject to subpoena or lawsuit for which we no longer have business purpose/relationship in connection with.  We do require the destruction or return of emails.  But we don’t require a scrub of backup media/hard drives/servers. We should not allow companies to keep a copy of our Confidential Information for “compliance with the NDA” or for “evidentiary purposes”. If the request is well evidenced and validated, please make a service desk ticket to legal advising the need for this change if you have commercial approval to make it.

clauses.issue: The other party wants a limitation on liability in this NDA to manage their risks. Bolt does not offer a limitation on liability in this NDA as this is a non-transactional document where there is no flow of money.
clauses.clauseExtract: Our primary concern is to seek an immediate injunction to prevent further non-disclosures and your co-operation in every reasonable way to help Bolt regain possession of such non-disclosure of the Confidential Information and prevent its further unauthorized use as specified in Section 5. With this in mind, trying to impose a limitation on liability is not necessarily the correct remedy for a breach of a non-disclosure agreement as this is not the immediate remedy that Bolt would take in the event of a breach. We do not want the parties to rely solely on financial compensation as the remedy for the breach. This is why we cannot accept your proposal for a limitation on liability.  Furthermore, there is no transaction (flow of money) between the parties therefore it is not equitable for the parties to rely on a limitation on liability.
fallbackPositions: If the position of not having a cap on liability is a showstopper, then escalate to legal through service desk for consideration.

clauses.issue: Other party requires penalties in the NDA.
clauses.clauseExtract: Generally we do not apply penalty clauses to low-risk NDAs. As Bolt is the only disclosing party we do not believe there should be any time limit required to make an appropriate disclosure nor should there be any penalty incurred should we delay in making such disclosures available.
fallbackPositions: None.

clauses.issue: The other party wants to change the term of the NDA to less than three (3) years.
fallbackPositions: You will have the option to accept a term of one, two, three, or five years at your own commercial discretion.
We are ok to sign off and say that it is fine to
We are ok with termination after 10 years
nonPermissibleDilutions: termination of contract can be triggered one way by provider whenever they wish

clauses.issue: Other party asks for indefinite trade secret protection.
fallbackPositions: This is okay provided the other party identifies the information that constitutes a trade secret. Please make a ticket to the legal in service desk for support amending this provision.

clauses.issue: Other party wants Bolt to warrant the accuracy and completeness of the Confidential Information or, if we will not, then require the removal of this section.
clauses.clauseExtract: Bolt will not accept any amendment to this warranty exclusion relating to the accuracy or completeness of the Confidential Information. The standard NDA relates to all business and operational discussions and disclosures therefore not tied to any-one particular purpose between the parties. Therefore we cannot completely warrant every discussion or disclosure made in relation to scoping activities etc. Bolt is also a fast-moving business that is innovating all the time so there could be changes to any information that we disclose because of the pace the business. Information could become outdated or obsolete quickly and therefore the line of communication should be open between the parties to work together co-operatively.
fallbackPositions: None.

clauses.issue: exclamation markTopic 1: Other party requests to supersede or invalidate a previous NDA.
fallbackPositions: The necessity for this type of language should be evaluated case by case. Please make a legal service desk ticket.

clauses.issue: exclamation markTopic 2: Other party wishes to make the NDA freely assignable.
fallbackPositions: The form requires consent to assign to a non-Affiliate third party, which would include a third party that acquires the assets of the other party. The reason for this is that we don’t want an unknown third party to which the NDA may be assigned to try to enforce obligations against us.  We will, however, allow assignment to a purchaser as a fallback position.  Please make a legal service desk ticket for support here.

clauses.issue: exclamation markTopic 3: Other party wants the NDA to be pursuant to their local law.
fallbackPositions: Bolt will accept an alternative jurisdiction where Bolt has a legal entity established if absolutely necessary. However, our standard should always be Estonia and we should try to maintain this option as a first choice.

clauses.issue: exclamation markTopic 4: The following are frequently requested additions that can be agreed at your commercial discretion for inclusion: Please make a service desk ticket to legal advising the additions needed once commercial approval to make it has been obtained.
exclamation markTopic 5: Other party wishes to include as-is and no warranty language.
fallbackPositions: Okay to accept this type of language. Please make a service desk ticket to legal advising the additions needed once commercial approval to make it has been obtained.

clauses.issue: exclamation markTopic 6: Other party wishes to include the right to attorney’s fees associated with disputes.
fallbackPositions: No fallback. We do not address legal fees in NDAs. We feel that they are unnecessary unless a subsequent definitive agreement is in place.  At this stage, both parties should be concerned with protecting disclosures of Confidential Information and not litigating.

clauses.issue: exclamation markTopic 7: Party wants to include “feedback” as an item of Confidential Information.
fallbackPositions: No fallback. Feedback is given by either party freely/voluntarily and is not considered Confidential Information. Additional language can be included to clarify the treatment of feedback in the Mutual NDA. Please make a service desk ticket to legal advising the additions needed once commercial approval to make it has been obtained.

hard_stop.label: Hard Stop
hard_stop.description: Raise to legal via Jira SD ticket. Do not negotiate — this is a blocker.

negotiate.label: Negotiate
negotiate.description: Apply fallback wording if available. Raise Jira ticket to track negotiation.

acceptable.label: Acceptable
acceptable.description: Minor deviation. Document it. No action required.

rules.action: Raise a ticket with Privacy Legal team
